target_customer: Small businesses and startups that want to buy manufactured products from Chinese vendors without finding suppliers themselves
problem: Finding and vetting Chinese suppliers and getting comparable quotes is slow and confusing for foreign buyers.
business_model: Procurement concierge service. A third-party directory lists pricing from 49 USD per month, which is unverified and may be outdated.

founders.name: Jack Wang
founders.background_notes: The YC page lists him as the only founder and gives no background. A separate Jack Wang who is a venture partner was not linked to this company and is ignored.

technical_complexity.rationale: A request intake and quote routing workflow with human sourcing agents behind it. The hard part was operations and vendor verification in China, not software.

defensibility.rationale: A concierge service built on a vendor network is easy to copy, and the YC description shows no proprietary data or lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source describes any incumbent response. Large marketplaces already offered supplier discovery, but the evidence for that is general, not tied to this company.

market_need_then: Foreign buyers sourcing from China is a large, long-standing activity, but no dated source in this search documents demand specific to this company.

branding.domain_note: sourcebeacon.com now redirects to a domain-name broker listing, so the original domain was dropped and is for sale. The YC page links a Crunchbase profile under the name Melotic, which may be a former or related name; this is unconfirmed.

brand_strength.rationale: No press, community or brand material was found, and a branding search returned only unrelated companies named Beacon.

outcome_analysis: The YC directory marks SourceBeacon as inactive, but no news item, post-mortem or founder statement explains why, so the cause of failure is not public. The only funding signal is a Crunchbase listing of four backers with no amounts or dates, which fits a small seed. A people-heavy concierge model with no visible moat and a small team of five would face thin margins, but that inference is not sourced, so no failure factors are recorded.
notes: Company website redirects to a domain broker page, so the site is dead. Investors come from a single Crunchbase snippet (one database); no amount or date was found, so the round is recorded with nulls. Dated competitor search found no rivals around the 2017 batch; an unrelated W17 company, Source.com, and a W18 company, Sourcify, are not comparable or are too late. Founder background and education were not found in any opened source.
